newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's A$8 billion a year coal industry is in crisis because of sharp falls in market prices, intense offshore competition, and a saturated market. As coal producers are struggling to break even, several companies have cut their workforce up to 40 pr cent, and thermal coal spot prices have hit their lowest levels in 10 years. Page 1.

Cable & Wireless, a key shareholder in Optus Communications, has approached the Federal Government over plans to restructure the troubled communications company which would see it buy out the other foreign shareholder in the company Bell South. Meanwhile British Telecom has also emerged as a possible investor in the restructured Optus. Page 35

Telstra has been offered full equity status in AT&T's global alliance WorldPartners. The offer by the world's second largest telecommunications company comes as Telstra has been considering an alternative offer from the BT-MCI alliance Concert, yet informed sources believe Telstra will not take the Concert deal. Page 35

New Zealand-based investor Brierley Investments executive director Rodney Price said the company, which has acquired 22.1 per cent of John Fairfax Holdings over the past week at a cost of A$52 million, is still keen to increase its stake in the publisher to the 25 per cent maximum stake allowed. Page 39

As predictions for its full year profit result, to be announced today, are spread between A$1.3 billion and A$1.4 billion, BHP Co Ltd have revealed a new plan to once again lift copper ore production and treatment capacity at the giant Escondida mine in Cile. Page 35.

Global media group News Corporation Ltd has come under attack from the Australian Stock Exchange over concerns it is in breach of the continuous disclosure rules over recent announcements made in the United States. Rupert Murdoch's News Corp derives most of its income from overseas, but maintains its primary listing here. Page 38.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's largest insurer, motoring group NRMA, yesterday prepared itself for entry into the financial services market with the A$60 million purchase of MLC Building Society. The deal will allow NRMA to offer a range of financial services, such as homeloans and superannuation, under its own name. Page 21.

While still facing an Australian Securities Commission inquiry into the active trading of shares in John Fairfax Holdings over the past few weeks, Brierley Investments yesterday confirmed it had used the creep provisions of the Corporations Law to increase its stake in Fairfax to 22 per cent. Page 21.

With the Productivity Commission due to release its report into the textile, clothing and footwear industry next week, British shoe group C&J Clark's global chief executive Timothy Parker warned the group may cease manufacturing in Australia if the Federa Government decides to reduce tariff protection for the industry after 2000. Page 21.

RGC managing director Mark Bethwaite said yesterday the company expects its net profit for 1996-97 to be half that of last year's because of weak tin prices and poor performances at the Thalanga and Renison base metal mines. The news of the profit slump sent RGC down 13 cents to A$4.87. Page 22.

WMC managing director Hugh Morgan yesterday backed the Federal Government's stance on greenhouse gas emission targets, saying Australia would face an unreasonable burden from uniform targets, and predicting economic growth would be worse than Prime Ministr John Howard's forecast of 2 per cent of GDP. Page 22.

In the first of a number of writedowns expected to be announced today, BHP will sell Newcastle's electrolytic manganese dioxide plant for A$57 million after signing a memorandum of understanding with South African-based Delta Electrical Industries, takinga A$49 million writedown on the sale. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Wesfarmers managing director Michael Chaney and finance director Eric Fraunschiel have been unsuccessful in talks with ICI Australia's British parent company ICI plc, and have abandoned plans for Wesfarmers' A$3.5 billion takeover bid of ICI. The bid woud have created Australia's largest diversified industrial group. Page 25.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston has refused to confirm whether he has been approached to relax the foreign ownership rules in Optus' licence in a move that would see the United Kingdom's Cable & Wireless to take majority control and provide an exit strategy for other shareholders. Page 25.

Insurer NRMA paid Lend Lease A$60 million for the MLC Building Society, a move that will see NRMA become a player in Australia's A$180 billion home lending market. The NRMA will leverage off its 2.35 million member base by supplying MLC products and servces through its extensive branch network under its own name. Page 25.

New Zealand-based investment group Brierley Investments revealed yesterday it raised its stake in John Fairfax Holdings to 22.1 per cent, a move that is under investigation by the Australian Securities Commission. The purchase lifts Brierley's average prce for its Fairfax shares from A$2.82 to A$2.86 each. Page 25.

A survey released yesterday and produced by the Australian Institute of Petroleum shows Australian oil companies are running empty and to ensure sustainable profit they may be forced to close refineries and thousands of petrol stations. The survey showeda return of just 5.2 per cent on the A$11 billion invested by the four major oil companies. Page 27.

After boosting the first-year income yield of the planned Envestra float from 7.2 per cent to 7.75 per cent after an initial poor response from institutional investors, Boral will today secure on early indication of institutional interest in its energy spin-off company. Page 27.
THE AGE

British communications giant Cable & Wireless, which currently owns 24.5 per cent of Optus, is expected to next week seek Federal Government approval to list its stake above the 49 per cent foreign-ownership limit. It is understood C&W are negotiating to buy a further 24.5 per cent in Optus from United States shareholder BellSouth. Page B1

Clarks Shoes have threatened to close their remaining Australian manufacturing operations in Collingwood and Geelong, which together employ 100 people, if the Federal Government takes up the expected recommendations of the Industry Commission report, due n Monday. The report, into the textile, clothing and footwear industries, is expected to recommend continued tariff cuts beyond 2000. Page B1

In a notice to the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, Brierley Investments confirmed it was the mystery buyer behind stockbroker HSBC James Capel's purchase of 16 million shares in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings. BIL said it bought 7.5 millin ordinary shares for A$24.6 million on June 17, and 8.5 million shares for A$27.3 million on 24 June. Page B2.

The proposed takeover of ICI Austraia by Wesfarmers has fallen through because of failed negotiations with ICI's British parent company ICI plc. Sources close to the parties said Wesfarmers was not prepared to pay the current market price for ICIA, which has been on the rise for the past few weeks. Page B3.

Australian Institute of Petroleum executive director Jim Starkey says cheap imports from Asia, along with fierce local competition and overregulation has stifled profits for Australian oil companies. Starkey said many petrol retailers, who may have to be closed down, were making more money out of selling soft drinks than selling petrol. Page B3.

While analysts said yesterday New Zealand businessman Graeme Hart looked ready to make a bid for Burns Philp & Co after notifying the company he wished to increase his 19.9 per cent stake, it was unclear whether Hart and his Rank Group needed a partner to make a bid and how long it would take. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
